questions.question: What is a solution of a system of inequalities?
choices: A value that satisfies only the first inequality
The intercept of any boundary line
Any point on an unshaded region
A value or point that satisfies every inequality

questions.question: What type of boundary line represents y > 2x + 1?
What type of boundary line represents y ≤ −x + 4?
For y > x, which side of the boundary y = x is shaded?
Which point satisfies both x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0?
What region represents the solution of two graphed inequalities?
choices: The overlap of their solution regions
Every point in either region, even without overlap

questions.question: Which symbol includes equality?
Why is a dashed boundary excluded from the solution set?
Which point satisfies y ≥ 2x and y ≤ x + 3?
Does (0, 0) satisfy both y > x − 1 and y < 3?
choices: No, because it is on both boundaries
No, because zero cannot satisfy strict inequalities
Yes, because the origin satisfies every system

questions.question: What does x ≥ 0 mean in a budget model where x counts items?
choices: The number of items must be positive
The number of items cannot be negative
The number of items can be any negative integer
The number of items must equal zero

questions.question: Which system describes points above y = 2 and below y = 5, excluding both boundaries?
Why do y > 4 and y < 1 have no shared solutions?
choices: The two boundaries have different slopes
A system must include x to have solutions
No y-value can satisfy both conditions
